master_prompt: Correct the anatomical errors in the input image while preserving the original character identity, art style, pose intention, composition, lighting, colors, clothing, accessories, and overall mood. This is a strict ANATOMY CORRECTION task, not a style conversion or creative redesign. Keep the image as visually close to the original as possible, but repair distorted anatomy, incorrect proportions, malformed hands, extra or missing fingers, unnatural joints, broken limb alignment, warped facial structure, asymmetry errors, and body balance issues. The final result must look like the same image after a professional anatomy cleanup pass.

meta.avoid: style change, redesign, new pose, new outfit, new character, different face, different rendering style

rules: Preserve the original character identity, pose intention, silhouette, composition, framing, color palette, lighting, rendering style, and mood
User text instructions override the original image only when they explicitly describe anatomical corrections or preservation priorities
If no text instructions are provided, only repair visible anatomical mistakes while keeping all artistic choices unchanged
Do not introduce new character traits, new props, new clothing, new background elements, or a different art style

user_input_override.instruction: All user-defined anatomy corrections and preservation instructions must be fully integrated.

step_1_original_image_analysis: Identify the original art style, rendering method, line quality, shading, palette, lighting direction, and finish
Identify the character's physical traits, face structure, expression, hairstyle, body type, clothing, accessories, and pose intention
Identify the composition, camera angle, perspective, crop, background, and focal point
Identify all anatomical errors without changing correct or intentional stylized features
step_2_anatomy_diagnosis: Check head-to-body proportion, neck placement, shoulder width, torso length, pelvis alignment, limb length, joint placement, and body balance
Check arms, elbows, wrists, legs, knees, ankles, hands, fingers, feet, and visible joints for deformation or unnatural bends
Check hand anatomy for exactly 5 fingers per hand when visible, natural finger spacing, correct knuckles, believable palm structure, and natural wrist alignment
Check facial anatomy for eye alignment, nose and mouth placement, jaw shape, cheek structure, ear placement, and expression consistency
Check perspective consistency so foreshortened limbs remain believable without becoming tangled, melted, stretched, or broken
step_3_correction_application: Repair only the anatomical mistakes while preserving the original pose intention
Adjust proportions subtly so the character remains recognizable and stylistically consistent
Correct hands and fingers with clear natural structure, avoiding fused digits, extra fingers, missing fingers, or claw-like deformation
Correct limb alignment and joint placement while keeping the original gesture and silhouette as close as possible
Correct facial structure only enough to remove distortion while preserving the original face identity, expression, and face shape
Preserve the original clothing design and adapt folds only where anatomy correction requires it
Preserve the original lighting, shadows, color palette, brushwork, lineart, and texture style

style_preservation.description: The corrected image must retain the same visual style as the input image.
rules: Do not convert the image into anime, comic, photorealistic, painterly, 3D, or any other style unless the original already uses that style
Do not add more detail than the original image supports
Do not simplify, beautify, age, de-age, or redesign the character
Do not change the character's species, gender presentation, body type, ethnicity, outfit, props, hairstyle, or expression unless explicitly requested
Do not change the background, camera angle, crop, or composition unless required to fix anatomy

pose_preservation.description: Maintain the original pose intention while making it anatomically believable.
rules: Keep the same action line, gesture, attitude, and emotional tone
Avoid replacing the pose with a generic safe pose
Avoid extreme pose changes unless the original anatomy is impossible to repair otherwise
Maintain silhouette readability and character-background separation
Keep visible hands visible whenever possible

body: Correct humanoid proportions according to the original stylization level
Maintain believable skeletal structure beneath the stylized design
Align head, neck, shoulders, ribcage, pelvis, and limbs naturally
Fix twisted torsos, broken spines, misplaced shoulders, floating limbs, uneven limb lengths, and collapsed body balance
Respect perspective and foreshortening without allowing distortion
hands: Exactly 5 fingers per visible hand unless the character design explicitly has a different anatomy
Correct palm structure, thumb placement, knuckle rhythm, finger taper, and finger length hierarchy
No fused fingers, extra fingers, missing fingers, rubber fingers, claw hands, or melted hands
Hands should support the original gesture and object interaction
face: Preserve the original face identity and face shape
Correct distorted facial symmetry while keeping natural expression
Align eyes, brows, nose, mouth, jaw, ears, and hairline believably
Avoid changing the character into a different person
clothing_and_props: Preserve all clothing, armor, props, weapons, accessories, and materials
Adjust fabric folds only where corrected anatomy requires it
Keep props correctly gripped, worn, or attached to the body
Do not add or remove equipment unless explicitly requested

image_quality: same art style as the input
composition: preserve the character as the main focal point
avoid introducing clutter or new narrative elements

internal_generation_logic: Perform a professional anatomy cleanup pass on the input image. First preserve the original style, identity, pose intention, composition, color palette, lighting, and mood. Then correct anatomical mistakes only where they appear: hands, fingers, limbs, joints, torso, neck, face structure, balance, and perspective. Keep every correction subtle and faithful so the final image feels like the same artwork with repaired anatomy, not a new illustration.
final_output_instruction: Generate only the corrected final image. Do not explain the process.
